comparison: Qwen2.5-Coder native Q4_K_M versus its own Transformers FP16 checkpoint
caveat: Runtime and precision differ; not a pure quantization ablation

losses.evidence: Q4 maps any negative input to GCD(0,0), returning zero. Hidden tests report GCD(-12,18), GCD(12,-18), and GCD(-12,-18) = 0, want 6. Both compile.
After the same merge implementation and return, Q4 adds example dictionaries and ends inside an opening string at the cap. Compiler reports unterminated string literal.
Q4 adds iterative and second recursive factorial functions after the target, then reaches the cap inside ValueError's string. Compiler reports unterminated string literal.
Both outputs start with the same loop completion. Q4 then adds a top-level print; the unchanged suffix produces an unexpected indent at line 10. This is not an inference transport error.
After a FizzBuzz expression, Q4 adds fizzbuzz_generator and stops at 'for i'. Compiler reports invalid syntax.
Both outputs contain GCD and LCM. Q4 additionally generates an interactive main function and ends inside the __main__ string. Compiler reports unterminated string literal.

gains.evidence: Both return the same recursive factorial expression. FP16 adds console.log(factorial(5)); its completed function plus the unchanged suffix produces Unexpected token '}' at line 13. Q4 adds extra factorial functions, with the suffix closing the last one, and the actual fixture passes and prints 'ok'. Extra code is not uniformly fatal; strict outcomes depend on the unchanged fixture contract.

Both implement division-by-zero checking. FP16 continues into another unfinished function declaration at the cap; the compiler reports expected an indented block after function definition on line 15. Q4 ends after a complete example try/except and passes the actual fixture despite printing 'Result: 5.0'.
